label: accepted

evidence.V1: Reads as a mossy boulder from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette; outline is an irregular faceted lozenge with no ambiguous angle.
evidence.V2: Only one big form plus a moss cap; the small companion pebble is visible only from the top view and hidden in front/three-quarter, so medium and small detail barely register.
evidence.V3: Generic squat lozenge with an evenly flattened plateau top and similar-sized facets; reads as a stock low-poly rock rather than a confidently stylised one (no strong lean, overhang or chunky secondary planes).
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with crisp breaks between the lit top planes and the dark sides; facet edges catch light consistently in the side-facet close-up.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups show clean designed facets with no pinches, holes or z-fighting; only faint smoothing streaks along facet ridges, within the designed-facet look.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in two to three values plus a single moss green: disciplined; sandstone and redrock colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 308 tris vs rock target 400 / ceiling 1000: under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, rock with designed flat facets and a leaf-green moss secondary as the Nature spec asks.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct for static scenery.

artifacts: faint smoothing streaks along some facet ridges (minor, within designed-facet style)
top_fixes: Push the silhouette: add a lean or overhang and vary facet sizes (a few big planes, some small chips) so it reads as a stylised boulder, not a generic lozenge
Move the companion pebble to the front/side where it is visible from the main angles, or add a second visible chunk, to create medium/small hierarchy
Make the moss cap follow the form with a soft-edged, slightly raised patch instead of a flat face fill with a hard triangular wedge down the side
